english.title: Attempt sexual assault on a female - SOA 2003
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) intentionally attempted to touch a

(A)_[girl aged13]_
(B)_[girl aged14]_
(C)_[girl aged15]_
(D)_[woman aged 16 or over]_

and that touching would have been sexual she would not have consented and you did not reasonably believe that she would have consented
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) of the Criminal Attempts Act 1981.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
intentionally attempted to touch a girl aged 13/14/15/woman aged 16 or over
by touching her body that touching would have been sexual
you not reasonably believing that she would consent

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Where the victim of the assault is a girl under 13 use CJS Code SX03017 and H5673.
(ii) See section 72 of, and Schedule 2 to, the Sexual Offences Act 2003 regarding the committing of this offence outside the UK by UK nationals / residents.
(iii) A person guilty of this offence is subject to notification and orders as provided by section 80 of the Act. (Sch 3 paragraph 19).
(vi) Whether a belief is reasonable is to be determined having regard to all the circumstances, including any steps the offender has taken to ascertain whether the victim consented - (section 3(2)).
(v) See also offence wordings: H5662 - which relates to this offence against a male and H5673 for the offence against a girl under 13.
(vi) The Court of Appeal case R v H (The Times 08/02/05) held that (that in those particular circumstances) a defendant who grabbed at the tracksuit bottoms worn by a female complainant had touched another person for the purpose of a sexual assault.
(vii) Where this offence is committed against an emergency worker this must be treated as an aggravating factor in sentencing, see section 67 of the Sentencing Act 2020.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: Ten years imprisonment

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
